items.title: datasette #3046: Don't serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages
items.summary: datasette #3046: Don't serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages I was looking at the Firefox network panel today when I noticed that requests to a Datasette table page were triggering an HTTP prefetch to the next page of rows in that table. This was happening because Datasette pages serve an HTTP link header like this: link: <https://latest.datasette.io/fixtures/compound_three_primary_keys?_next=a%2Cd%2Cv>; rel="next" This is bad. A tiny fraction of the visitors to one of those pages will click the "next" link, which means their browser is fetching unnecessary data and the Datasette server is having to render an entire page that then gets thrown away. I dug in and learned that Firefox has an issue that has been open for 24 years about this behavior... And one of the early comments on that issue links to my blog post from 2002 complaining about this feature. I hadn't just forgotten that I had written about it, I had forgotten the feature entirely! Tags: firefox , html , mozilla , datasette

it.title: È questa l'IA che vogliamo? Accelerazione, mercati e VC

L'episodio si concentra sui recenti rapporti e sul documento pubblicato da METR riguardo alla velocità con cui l'intelligenza artificiale sta già accelerando la ricerca interna ad Anthropic. I conduttori, tra cui Prakash Narayanan, esaminano le implicazioni di questa rapida evoluzione tecnologica.

Vengono inoltre esplorati temi di mercato e finanziari, come le scommesse sulle elezioni legate all'IA, il trading di GPU e l'ascesa del venture capital orientato esclusivamente all'intelligenza artificiale, offrendo una panoramica completa dei cambiamenti in atto.
it.context: Il dibattito sull'accelerazione dell'IA e sui suoi effetti collaterali economici e operativi si inserisce in un panorama in cui i progressi tecnici e i finanziamenti si muovono a ritmi senza precedenti.

Nel panorama della sicurezza informatica legata all'intelligenza artificiale, la cooperazione tra aziende leader e specialisti del settore rappresenta un passo cruciale. La partnership con Hacktron si concentra sull'identificazione proattiva delle vulnerabilità e sulla verifica delle connessioni con servizi esterni.

Osservare l'evoluzione di queste iniziative di sicurezza è fondamentale per comprendere come le organizzazioni intendano proteggere le infrastrutture complesse basate su modelli di frontiera. Nei prossimi sviluppi sarà importante monitorare i risultati concreti di questa cooperazione in termini di resilienza dei sistemi.

Observers will monitor how widely this benchmark is adopted and whether it effectively captures the complexities of real-world laboratory workflows, distinguishing project claims from verified performance.

es.why_it_matters: Proporciona un marco estructurado para evaluar el desempeño de la inteligencia artificial en tareas científicas prácticas y cotidianas.

La intersección entre la inteligencia artificial y la investigación científica requiere herramientas de evaluación rigurosas. BioBasicsBench busca medir cómo los agentes manejan datos experimentales sin procesar a través de cien tareas estandarizadas.

El desarrollo continuo de estos puntos de referencia permitirá a la comunidad examinar el progreso real de los agentes autónomos en entornos de laboratorio húmedo.
es.context: El uso de agentes inteligentes en la investigación científica impulsa la necesidad de crear pruebas estandarizadas para medir su competencia técnica.

items.summary: Hello, and welcome back to The Cognitive Revolution. Today, my guest is Joshua Monrad, co-founder and managing director of Sentinel Bio, a biosecurity nonprofit and grant maker that's working to make pandemics history within our lifetimes, and until recently, also a biosecurity advisor at the OpenAI Foundation.

it.title: Dalla KYC alla KYA: biose sicurezza e screening del DNA con Sentinel Bio

La discussione esplora lo screening del DNA, gli studi di uplift e il monitoraggio degli agenti biologici per prevenire le pandemie.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere le strategie di biosecurity e il passaggio dai controlli KYC tradizionali alla KYA (Know Your Agent/Asset) offre uno sguardo cruciale sulla prevenzione dei rischi pandemici futuri.
it.extended_analysis:
Il panorama della sicurezza biologica sta subendo profonde trasformazioni, guidato da organizzazioni come Sentinel Bio che operano per rendere le pandemie un ricordo del passato. Attraverso il lavoro di Joshua Monrad, ex consulente di biosecurity presso la OpenAI Foundation e co-fondatore della no-profit, emergono temi chiave come lo screening del DNA e il monitoraggio degli agenti biologici.

L'episodio esamina il concetto di KYA in relazione alla sicurezza tecnologica e biologica, offrendo spunti di riflessione sulle implicazioni della ricerca e sugli studi di uplift. Gli ascoltatori possono esplorare come la prevenzione attiva e la governance della ricerca biologica si intersegano con lo sviluppo tecnologico moderno.
it.context: Il podcast The Cognitive Revolution esplora le frontiere dell'intelligenza artificiale e della tecnologia. In questo episodio, l'attenzione si sposta sulla convergenza tra biosecurity, prevenzione delle pandemie e monitoraggio avanzato.
key_takeaways: Joshua Monrad discute il passaggio dai tradizionali controlli KYC alle pratiche KYA nella biosecurity.
Sentinel Bio opera come organizzazione no-profit e grant maker focalizzata sulla prevenzione delle pandemie.

it.title: Le università australiane puntano a laureati 'AI-native'
it.summary: Gli atenei australiani stanno estendendo l'accesso a ChatGPT e integrando l'intelligenza artificiale nella didattica. L'obiettivo è preparare gli studenti a un mercato del lavoro sempre più orientato all'IA.
it.why_it_matters: L'iniziativa mostra come l'istruzione superiore stia modificando i propri programmi per rispondere alla diffusione dell'IA nel mondo professionale.
it.extended_analysis:
Le istituzioni universitarie in Australia stanno modificando l'approccio educativo espandendo l'uso di strumenti come ChatGPT direttamente nei percorsi di studio. Questa mossa mira a formare una nuova generazione di professionisti capaci di operare con disinvoltura in contesti lavorativi digitali avanzati.

Sebbene i dettagli completi sui curricula non siano specificati, l'iniziativa riflette una tendenza globale volta a ripensare la didattica di fronte ai progressi tecnologici.
it.context: Il mondo accademico affronta la sfida di adattare la formazione alle competenze richieste da un mercato del lavoro che adotta rapidamente sistemi di intelligenza artificiale generativa.
key_takeaways: Estensione dell'accesso a ChatGPT nelle università australiane
Integrazione dell'IA nella didattica e nei metodi di insegnamento
Preparazione degli studenti per la forza lavoro del futuro
highlights: Coinvolgimento delle università australiane
Focus sull'utilizzo di strumenti basati su IA

en.title: Australian universities shape AI-native graduates
en.summary: Australian universities are expanding access to ChatGPT and embedding artificial intelligence into teaching and learning. This effort aims to equip students for an AI-enabled workforce.
en.why_it_matters: This move highlights how higher education is adapting its academic frameworks to address the integration of AI across professional industries.
en.extended_analysis:
Higher education institutions across Australia are broadening access to platforms like ChatGPT to incorporate artificial intelligence directly into the learning experience. By doing so, they seek to prepare students for modern career environments shaped by automation and advanced digital tools.

While specific course structures vary, the trend underscores a broader institutional shift toward embracing generative technology in mainstream education rather than restricting it.
en.context: Educational bodies globally are rethinking assessment and curriculum design to keep pace with rapid advancements in generative artificial intelligence technologies.
key_takeaways: Expansion of ChatGPT access across Australian campuses
Embedding artificial intelligence into teaching practices
Preparing graduates for an AI-driven professional workforce
highlights: Initiative led by Australian universities
Partnership or adoption reported via OpenAI News

es.title: Universidades australianas forman graduados nativos en IA
es.summary: Las universidades de Australia están ampliando el acceso a ChatGPT e integrando la inteligencia artificial en la enseñanza. La iniciativa busca preparar a los estudiantes para un mercado laboral digital.
es.why_it_matters: Muestra cómo el sector educativo superior adapta sus métodos para responder a la presencia de la IA en los entornos profesionales.
es.extended_analysis:
Las instituciones académicas australianas están incorporando herramientas como ChatGPT en sus aulas para enriquecer los procesos de enseñanza y aprendizaje. El propósito principal es dotar a los estudiantes de competencias prácticas para un entorno laboral transformado por la tecnología.

Esta evolución institucional marca un cambio importante respecto a las restricciones iniciales impuestas a las herramientas generativas en el ámbito educativo.
es.context: El sistema educativo internacional debate cómo integrar de manera constructiva las tecnologías de inteligencia artificial en los planes de estudio universitarios.
key_takeaways: Ampliación del acceso a ChatGPT en el ámbito universitario australiano
Integración de la inteligencia artificial en la enseñanza y el aprendizaje
Enfoque en la empleabilidad y preparación para el entorno laboral
highlights: Impulso en universidades de Australia
Adaptación de la enseñanza académica

澳大利亚的高等教育机构正在通过引入ChatGPT等平台，将人工智能技术直接嵌入教学与学习环节。通过这种方式，校方希望帮助学生掌握现代职场所需要的数字化技能。

de.why_it_matters: Die Entwicklung verdeutlicht, wie das Hochschulwesen seine Programme anpasst, um auf den Einsatz von KI in der Berufswelt zu reagieren.

Universitäten in Australien erweitern die Nutzung von Plattformen wie ChatGPT, um künstliche Intelligenz direkt in den Lernprozess einzubinden. Ziel ist es, Studierende optimal auf moderne berufliche Anforderungen vorzubereiten, die stark von digitalen Technologien beeinflusst werden.

Diese Anpassung zeigt einen Wandel hin zur aktiven Integration generativer Werkzeuge in die akademische Ausbildung anstelle von restriktiven Maßnahmen.
de.context: Bildungseinrichtungen weltweit stehen vor der Aufgabe, Curricula und Lehrmethoden im Einklang mit den schnellen Fortschritten der künstlichen Intelligenz weiterzuentwickeln.

Integration von künstlicher Intelligenz in die Lehre

it.title: Intelligenza artificiale al Midwest AI Summit: parte seconda
it.summary: In questo episodio speciale, tre interventi dal Midwest AI Summit analizzano come le organizzazioni applicano l'intelligenza artificiale. Vengono trattati la definizione di confini operativi tramite charter dedicate, la gestione dei processi decisionali interni e l'uso pratico di agenti autonomi e modelli di visione.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere le strategie organizzative è fondamentale per integrare l'intelligenza artificiale in modo sicuro ed efficiente, definendo chiare responsabilità e confini etici e operativi.
it.extended_analysis: L'episodio approfondisce l'implementazione pratica dell'intelligenza artificiale attraverso casi di studio aziendali e istituzionali presentati al Midwest AI Summit. Don Barger spiega il valore di una carta etica per stabilire limiti d'uso, Mark Lay affronta le decisioni gestionali chiave come il debito tecnico e la delega, mentre Darren Taillie mostra l'impiego concreto di modelli di visione e agenti per automatizzare i processi lavorativi.
it.context: Il panorama attuale richiede alle organizzazioni di passare dalla sperimentazione teorica all'adozione strutturata di sistemi basati sull'intelligenza artificiale, affrontando sfide di governance e automazione operativa.
key_takeaways: L'importanza di stabilire una carta di governance per definire limiti e usi consentiti dell'IA.
La gestione del debito tecnico e delle responsabilità decisionali all'interno delle organizzazioni.
L'applicazione pratica di agenti IA e modelli di visione per migliorare l'accesso ai dati e l'automazione.
highlights: Interventi di Don Barger, Mark Lay e Darren Taillie registrati al Midwest AI Summit.
Analisi dell'uso di agenti IA, text-to-SQL e modelli di visione per l'automazione.

en.title: Abundant Intelligence at the Midwest AI Summit Part 2
en.summary: This special episode features three talks from the Midwest AI Summit, exploring how organizations implement AI in practice. Guests discuss setting operational boundaries with charters, managing organizational AI decisions, and deploying AI agents and vision models for automation.
en.why_it_matters: Examining real-world organizational strategies helps leaders understand how to govern AI adoption, maintain human oversight, and streamline practical workflows safely.
en.extended_analysis: Drawing from presentations at the Midwest AI Summit, this episode highlights organizational approaches to artificial intelligence. Don Barger discusses creating an AI charter to set boundaries, Mark Lay examines structural decisions around accountability and technical debt, and Darren Taillie details practical implementations using text-to-SQL, AI agents, and vision models to automate tasks.
en.context: Organizations increasingly need robust governance frameworks and practical methodologies to transition from AI experimentation to scalable, controlled real-world deployment.
key_takeaways: Establishing formal AI charters helps organizations define clear boundaries and operational scope.
Managing AI across enterprises requires balancing accountability, delegation, and technical debt.
Teams are actively leveraging AI agents, vision models, and text-to-SQL to automate work order verification and data access.
highlights: Featured speakers include Don Barger, Mark Lay, and Darren Taillie.
Discussions cover practical deployment of AI agents and data access tools.

es.why_it_matters: Conocer los enfoques organizacionales permite a los líderes gestionar mejor la adopción de la inteligencia artificial, manteniendo el control humano y la eficiencia operativa.
es.extended_analysis: A través de las ponencias del evento, el episodio detalla cómo diferentes entidades abordan la gobernanza y la automatización. Don Barger aborda el uso de una carta de IA para definir directrices, Mark Lay explora la gestión y el debito técnico, y Darren Taillie muestra casos prácticos con modelos de visión y agentes para automatizar procesos.
es.context: El sector tecnológico y empresarial busca metodologías estables para alinear la adopción de la inteligencia artificial con estrictos marcos de gobernanza y responsabilidad corporativa.
key_takeaways: Las cartas de IA estructuran el uso adecuado y los límites de la tecnología en las entidades.
La gestión organizativa requiere atender la rendición de cuentas y el impacto técnico.
Los agentes y modelos de visión facilitan la automatización de flujos de trabajo específicos.
highlights: Participación de Don Barger, Mark Lay y Darren Taillie en el evento.
Ejemplos prácticos sobre el uso de text-to-SQL y modelos de visión.

团队正积极利用AI代理、视觉模型和文本转SQL技术来优化工作流程。

Don Barger erklärt den Nutzen einer KI-Charta zur Grenzziehung, Mark Lay beleuchtet Managemententscheidungen bezüglich technischer Schulden und Verantwortlichkeit, während Darren Taillie praktische Anwendungen von Vision-Modellen und KI-Agenten vorstellt.

items.title: GPT‑6 Cyber: Advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents

it.title: GPT-6 Cyber: il nuovo modello OpenAI per la sicurezza informatica
it.summary: OpenAI ha presentato GPT-6 Cyber, un modello di cybersecurity progettato per individuare vulnerabilità sfruttabili e creare correzioni, addestrato per operare entro limiti autorizzati.
it.why_it_matters: Questo modello esplora la frontiera degli agenti di sicurezza allineati, combinando la capacità di trovare falle critiche con lo sviluppo di contromisure mirate.
it.extended_analysis:
L'annuncio introduce GPT-6 Cyber come strumento specializzato nella ricerca di vulnerabilità e nella creazione di correzioni di sicurezza. La caratteristica centrale evidenziata riguarda l'addestramento volto a mantenere l'agente all'interno di uno scope autorizzato.

Nel contesto attuale della sicurezza informatica basata sull'intelligenza artificiale, l'equilibrio tra l'efficacia nell'individuare exploit e il controllo rigoroso dei confini operativi rappresenta una sfida cruciale per sviluppatori e organizzazioni.

Sarà importante osservare come evolveranno le applicazioni pratiche di questo modello e in che modo verranno validate le sue capacità di operare in modo sicuro ed etico sul campo.
it.context: Il panorama della sicurezza informatica vede una crescente adozione di modelli di IA avanzati per automatizzare sia l'analisi delle difese sia la ricerca di vulnerabilità complesse.
key_takeaways: GPT-6 Cyber è focalizzato sulla ricerca di vulnerabilità e sullo sviluppo di correzioni.
Il modello è stato addestrato per operare rigorosamente all'interno di uno scope autorizzato.
Rappresenta un progresso nella frontiera degli agenti di cybersecurity allineati.
highlights: Presentato da OpenAI News il 5 novembre 2026.
Progettato per trovare vulnerabilità e sviluppare fix.

en.title: GPT-6 Cyber: OpenAI's New Model for Cybersecurity Agents
en.summary: OpenAI has introduced GPT-6 Cyber, a specialized cybersecurity model built to discover exploitable vulnerabilities and develop fixes while remaining within authorized boundaries.
en.why_it_matters: It pushes the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents, balancing advanced exploit detection with strict adherence to authorized operational scopes.
en.extended_analysis:
The introduction of GPT-6 Cyber marks a significant step in developing AI models capable of handling complex security tasks, such as finding flaws and writing patches. Crucially, the model is trained to stay within authorized parameters.

As organizations increasingly turn to automated systems for defensive and offensive security analysis, ensuring robust alignment and boundary control remains paramount for preventing misuse.

Future developments will show how effectively these aligned cybersecurity agents can be integrated into standard enterprise workflows and security operations.
en.context: The cybersecurity sector is actively exploring how advanced language and reasoning models can assist security professionals in vulnerability management and remediation.
key_takeaways: Designed to identify exploitable vulnerabilities and develop code fixes.
Trained specifically to stay within authorized operational scopes.
Represents a development in aligned cybersecurity agent technology.
highlights: Announced by OpenAI News on November 5, 2026.
Focused on cybersecurity alignment and vulnerability management.

es.title: GPT-6 Cyber: el nuevo modelo de OpenAI para ciberseguridad
es.summary: OpenAI ha presentado GPT-6 Cyber, un modelo de ciberseguridad diseñado para encontrar vulnerabilidades explotables y desarrollar correcciones dentro de un ámbito autorizado.
es.why_it_matters: Este avance explora la frontera de los agentes de seguridad alineados, uniendo la detección de fallos complejos con un estricto control operativo.
es.extended_analysis:
La llegada de GPT-6 Cyber introduce un enfoque especializado para la detección de vulnerabilidades y la creación de soluciones de parcheo. El aspecto clave radica en su entrenamiento para operar estrictamente bajo un alcance autorizado.

En el ecosistema tecnológico actual, la automatización de la ciberseguridad mediante IA plantea importantes retos de control y alineación para evitar usos indebidos y garantizar la fiabilidad.

Será necesario observar cómo se implementa este modelo en entornos reales y qué medidas de verificación se adoptarán para asegurar su cumplimiento normativo.
es.context: La ciberseguridad basada en inteligencia artificial busca herramientas capaces de auditar códigos y sistemas complejos con mayor rapidez y precisión.
key_takeaways: Enfocado en la detección de vulnerabilidades explotables y desarrollo de correcciones.
Entrenado para mantenerse dentro de límites autorizados.
Avanza en la frontera de los agentes de seguridad alineados.
highlights: Publicado por OpenAI News el 5 de noviembre de 2026.
Modelo especializado en ciberseguridad y desarrollo de parches.

zh-CN.title: GPT-6 Cyber：OpenAI发布的网络安全模型
zh-CN.summary: OpenAI推出了GPT-6 Cyber，这是一个旨在发现可利用漏洞并开发修复程序的网络安全模型，经过训练可保持在授权范围内。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 该模型推进了对齐网络安全代理的前沿发展，平衡了复杂的漏洞检测与严格的授权边界控制。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
GPT-6 Cyber的发布标志着人工智能在处理网络安全任务（如寻找缺陷和编写修复补丁）方面迈出了新的一步。其核心特征在于经过专门训练，以确保操作不超出授权范围。

在当前的技术背景下，如何在提升安全分析效率的同时确保模型严格对齐和合规，是业界面临的核心议题。

未来需要关注该模型在实际环境中的应用方式及其安全边界验证机制的演变。
zh-CN.context: 网络安全行业正在积极探索如何利用先进的语言和推理模型来协助专业人员进行漏洞管理和防御分析。
key_takeaways: 专注于发现可利用的漏洞并开发修复代码。
经过专门训练以保持在授权的操作范围内。
代表了对齐网络安全代理技术的新进展。
highlights: 由OpenAI News于2026年11月5日发布。
致力于网络安全漏洞查找与修复开发。

de.title: GPT-6 Cyber: OpenAIs neues Modell für Cybersicherheit
de.summary: OpenAI hat GPT-6 Cyber vorgestellt, ein Cybersicherheitsmodell zum Finden ausnutzbarer Schwachstellen und Entwickeln von Korrekturen innerhalb autorisierter Grenzen.
de.why_it_matters: Es erweitert die Grenzen ausgerichteter Cybersicherheitsagenten, indem es präzise Schwachstellenerkennung mit strenger Einhaltung autorisierter Bereiche verbindet.
de.extended_analysis:
Die Ankündigung von GPT-6 Cyber bringt ein spezialisiertes Modell zur Identifizierung von Sicherheitslücken und Erstellung von Patches hervor. Ein zentraler Aspekt ist das Training, das sicherstellen soll, dass das System im autorisierten Rahmen bleibt.

Im Kontext der modernen IT-Sicherheit ist die Entwicklung von KI-Modellen, die sowohl mächtig in der Analyse als auch kontrollierbar in ihren Aktionen sind, von großer Bedeutung.

Es bleibt zu beobachten, wie sich der Einsatz dieses Modells in der Praxis gestaltet und wie die Einhaltung der Sicherheitsvorgaben kontinuierlich verifiziert wird.
de.context: Der Bereich der Cybersicherheit erforscht zunehmend den Einsatz fortschrittlicher KI-Agenten zur Automatisierung von Schwachstellenanalysen und Abwehrmechanismen.
key_takeaways: Fokussiert auf das Auffinden von Schwachstellen und Erstellen von Fixes.
Trainiert, um innerhalb eines autorisierten Geltungsbereichs zu bleiben.
Stellt einen Fortschritt bei ausgerichteten Sicherheitsagenten dar.
highlights: Veröffentlicht von OpenAI News am 5. November 2026.
Entwickelt für Cybersicherheitsanalysen und Schwachstellenbehebung.

it.title: OpenAI acquisisce Pierre Computer Company
it.summary: OpenAI ha annunciato l'acquisizione di Pierre Computer Company, Inc. L'operazione mira ad espandere gli strumenti di Codex dedicati alla costruzione, comprensione e revisione del codice software.

it.extended_analysis:
OpenAI ha ufficializzato l'acquisizione di Pierre Computer Company, integrando le competenze della startup per arricchire la suite di strumenti associati a Codex. La mossa evidenzia l'impegno costante dell'azienda nel potenziare il supporto agli sviluppatori, migliorando i flussi di lavoro per la creazione e la revisione del codice.

Nel contesto attuale del mercato dell'intelligenza artificiale generativa, gli strumenti di programmazione assistita rappresentano un terreno di forte competizione. L'integrazione di nuove tecnologie punta a rendere i modelli sempre più precisi ed efficaci nell'assistere gli ingegneri software.

Sarà importante monitorare come le funzionalità di Pierre verranno integrate concretamente all'interno degli ecosistemi esistenti di Codex e quali saranno i prossimi sviluppi annunciati da OpenAI.
it.context: L'acquisizione si inserisce nella strategia di OpenAI di espandere le proprie capacità tecniche nel settore degli strumenti per sviluppatori, un segmento chiave per l'adozione aziendale dell'IA.

L'obiettivo è espandere gli strumenti di Codex per il codice.
Migliorerà la costruzione, comprensione e revisione del software.

items.title: datasette-apps 0.3a0
items.summary: Release: datasette-apps 0.3a0 Datasette Apps adds support for hosting and editing custom HTML applications inside of Datasette. These can be created by hand, but it's easier to create them using LLMs via Datasette Agent . This release improves that integration: Apps can now be tagged in Datasette Agent chat messages by typing # , which autocompletes from the apps the user has permission to view. New app_add_stored_queries() and app_remove_stored_queries() tools let the agent manage which stored queries an app is allowed to call. Granting a write query requires approval from the user first. app_create() now checks that each requested stored query exists and that the user can view it, and asks the user to approve any write queries before the app is created. The "View app" buttons shown by the agent tools, and the links on # app references, now open the app full screen in the Datasette Agent panel. Tags: datasette , datasette-agent , datasette-apps

items.title: Can AI Invent or Just Help Scientists Work Faster? with Richard Socher - #783
items.summary: AI can help scientists write code, analyze data, and draft papers. But can it generate the ideas that lead to new discoveries? Richard Socher, former chief scientist at Salesforce, founder of You.com, and co-founder of Recursive, joins us to explore the move from AI assisting researchers to AI conducting research. Starting with AI improving AI, we examine what it takes to propose ideas, run experiments, and validate results, and how those capabilities could eventually accelerate discovery across biology, chemistry, and physics. The conversation covers Recursive’s reported results in model training and GPU kernel optimization, why fast verification matters, and how reward hacking complicates the search for real improvements. We also discuss the data and experimental infrastructure needed for broader scientific discovery, whether commercial incentives can keep increasingly capable systems aligned, and Richard’s vision for a “Eureka machine.” 🗒️ Full show notes: ⁠https://twimlai.com/go/783.

items.title: Palette: teaching a small model to build decks in your design language
Qwen 3.8 27B on my laptop can interpret model weights, too
items.summary: Yesterday's hot paper was Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights by Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang, and Omar Khattab. The paper (OK, the authors classify is as a "blog post", but it's paper-shaped) found that frontier models, in particular GPT-6 Astra, can both interpret and modify the raw weights of a machine learning model - literally a text description of the model containing a bunch of floating point numbers. I've been playing with one of the examples from the paper and I'm delighted to share that Qwen 3.8 27B running on my laptop can do this as well! Weight-Space Programming Here's the highlight from their abstract, describing impressive capabilities for GPT-6 Astra and coining the term Weight-Space Programming for when LLMs analyze and modify model weights: Just by looking at the raw weights, GPT-6 Astra can tell what a network was trained to do . And without any environment feedback, it has no trouble writing, from scratch, small game-playing networks that outplay networks trained with PPO for 100 million steps. Likewise, asked to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math without gradients, Astra identifies an issue in its weights causing reasoning loops that Qwen’s own model card warns about, and fixes this by natively editing 0.016% of the weights . With the same sampling settings, this weight correction raises MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1% and generalizes out of the box to instruction following, raising IFEval by 3x. All of this is possible without allowing Astra to write training loops. It uses its reasoning to figure out what each part of a neural network computes, or should compute, and changes the weights accordingly. We call this Weight-Space Programming . llm 0.37
items.summary: Release: llm 0.37 There's a lot of stuff in this new release of my LLM CLI tool and Python library, representing around two months of accumulated features and fixes. I added gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6.1-terra , plus a new llm openai endpoint add command to make it easier to configure additional models that use OpenAI-compatible endpoints. I switched the default model (if you have not set your own default) to gpt-6-luna - half the price of the previous default, gpt-5.6-luna . LLM's support for embeddings now accepts that different binary content may have different content-type - necessary for models like Gemini Embedding 2 , which can embed text, audio, images, and video. A lot of open source maintainers complain about a flood of AI-assisted PRs. LLM is my project that has been most affected by this and, to be honest, I'm not finding it to be a problem. That's mainly because I have Opus 5.5 or GPT-6 Astra help me with triage to spot the most useful fixes! This release includes fixes from 12 authors - almost all AI-assisted - and the burden of reviewing them wasn't nearly as great as I expected. I really see them as bug reports with attached examples - sometimes I land them, sometimes I implement my own fix. So thanks to 0d00ciallo0721 , ac1982 , Allen Flux , Bian Yuhan , Bishop Kammeraad , Chen Yufeiyang , Christopher Krah , Ethan Stoner , Jiachen Xie , Olamide Faniyan , Sharat Chandra Sai Boddu , nosmile99 for helping out with (or spending tokens on) this release! Tags: open-source , projects , ai , annotated-release-notes , generative-ai , llms , embeddings , llm

items.title: The U.S. Census Bureau and “Super Intelligence”
items.summary: I was reminded today of AI Adoption Rate Trending Down for Large Companies , a chart produced by Apollo Global Management in September 2025, which appeared to show a slowdown in U.S. corporate AI adoption based on numbers collected by the U.S. Census Bureau. At the time I used that chart to demonstrate GPT-5 data analysis , and then to experiment with Claude's new Code Interpreter . I decided to try running those numbers again to see what had changed over the past year, and in doing so learned that the Bureau has fallen foul of Executive Order 14434 , aka the asinine Super Intelligence one. First, the updated chart Every two weeks the U.S. Census Bureau runs a survey called the Business Trends and Outlook Survey (aka BTOS). Each time it goes to 200,000 businesses out of 1.2 million total - the surveyed group (a "panel") cycles such that an individual business only completes the survey every twelve weeks. The latest data is published on alternating Thursdays at 10am. I used the most recent numbers (published October 22, 2026) to create a new version ( GPT-6 Astra Extra High transcript ) of the AI adoption chart, updated to reflect both the last twelve months and a change that was made to the survey question sent out by the Bureau: Here's a link to the larger image . For comparison, here's that AI adoption chart from last year (my GPT-5 version): In September 2025 the largest (250+ employees) companies answered "yes" around 12% of the time to the question about whether they used AI in "producing goods or services". Under the new "any business function" wording, by February 2026, those same large companies answered "yes" around 30% of the time, and by October 2026 that had increased to around 40%. items.title: If in doubt, delete the uv.lock file
items.summary: I've been getting the occasional confusing Python dependency error since switching over to Python 3.15 and the rule I'm having to remember is: If in doubt, delete the uv.lock file Most of my projects are libraries which don't include a uv.lock file, since it's rude for a library dependency to lock versions for anything else that uses it. Running uv run pytest etc tends to leave uv.lock files lying around, which are listed in .gitignore and so do not get committed to my repositories. But... sometimes that uv.lock pins a version of a dependency that doesn't yet have a Python 3.15 wheel. An example from earlier today: error: Failed to build `watchfiles==1.1.1` cause: Call to `maturin.build_wheel` failed error: the configured Python interpreter version (3.15) is newer than PyO3's maximum supported version (3.14) Deleting that file and running uv run pytest again usually fixes the problem. Tags: uv , til , python

items.title: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts
items.summary: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts Parameter Labs describe an exploit they found against ChatGPT's implementation of the artifacts pattern (OpenAI used to call this "Canvas" but it looks like the latest revision is called HTML previews ), where interactive custom HTML apps are displayed in a sandboxed iframe. It's important that HTML in these stays tightly sandboxed to avoid untrusted code interacting with OpenAI APIs and accessing private data. Parameter found quite a complex attack chain. OpenAI use the MathLive JavaScript library as part of their graph support, and that library includes its own virtual keyboard , which can be triggered in the parent page via postMessage() from the sandboxed iframe. That message receiving code uses innerHTML , so anything that sends a message can add custom HTML to the parent - and there was no mechanism to prevent other sandboxed frames, including HTML preview frames, from calling that method. This meant untrusted code in an iframe could insert HTML, and while innerHTML doesn't directly execute script elements it could be used to inject a new iframe without sandbox restrictions. OpenAI’s CSP rules blocked inline scripts entirely, and only allowed script loading from a handful of domains, but one of those was YouTube - and the YouTube oEmbed endpoint could be used to reflect JavaScript back in a way that executed it. Once the attack had JavaScript execution on ChatGPT, it was trivial to fetch private user data from APIs and exfiltrate it via an image reference. The end result: you could create a ChatGPT share URL which, when visited by another signed-in user, could exfiltrate their private data or take actions on their behalf. items.title: dbreunig/nesformer
items.summary: dbreunig/nesformer Inspired by qwenputer by Divyansh Agrawal, Drew Breunig baked a working emulator for a Nintendo Entertainment System 6502 CPU into the weights of Qwen3.5-4B. You can now play NES ROMs such as Super Mario Bros (very slowly) running inside Qwen! In a comment on Hacker News Drew reveals the Opus 5.5 prompts he used to build this system: Read this article and any relevant source code: https://divagr.com/blog/qwenputer. Then explore if you could emulate the chip and ram in a Nintendo Entertainment System (as people do today with FPGAs in MISTRs) using this technique. If so, what size model would you have to build and if you could use smaller faster ones, could you get it to be at the standard clockspeed. Followed by: I think we should build it! Just for fun. It's okay if it's not fast. We want to be able to have the weights, and a cli to run them that we can point at a ROM. Apparently Opus found and then used this collection of conformance tests for the NES CPU released 15 years ago by Christopher Pow. Via Hacker News Tags: games , ai , generative-ai , llms , drew-breunig , qwen , conformance-suites

items.title: Building a multiplayer game world with autonomous Fable-class models
items.summary: How I Built the Most AI-Pilled Company in the World Don't be put off by the clickbait headline, this piece by Jacob Sansbury describing how they are building Spawn is a fascinating exploration of the bleeding edge of what's possible with agentic engineering against frontier models. Spawn is a massively multiplayer gaming environment where players can use prompts (to the in-game agent, Savi) to modify the game world. I fired it up on my phone for a few minutes and was able to prompt a castle into existence, then a dragon, then ride the dragon to fly around that castle. By Jacob's telling, Spawn is now being developed autonomously by a swarm of Fable-powered agents costing over $3 million in tokens per month ("we spend 30x payroll on AI tokens"). Our agents change the live code directly and ship to production hourly, so they read every error, bug report and metric themselves. About 60% of our work starts from a production error, a Savi bug report (Savi is the AI you build games with in Spawn), something odd in our logs, or a feature request. Savi files bugs herself. When a user hits one, or Savi hits one in the product, she files it. It goes straight to an agent that decides whether it's a real bug to fix, something we won't fix, or intentional design that needs a decision. Usually it becomes a change, delivered to that user within an hour, with a message in the same chat. This is continuous deployment turned up to 11: A loop this tight only works if it never stops, so we treat an hour without a ship as a SEV-0, our most severe kind of incident. Unshipped changes pile up, and every problem already in production lasts longer. The feedback slows down too. An agent can only keep a few hours of work in its head, so shipping faster than that actually helps it stay coherent. [.

en.title: OpenAI's Updated Model Spec Aims for Capable and Beneficial AI
en.summary: OpenAI has released an updated Model Spec outlining five core values to guide capable artificial intelligence. The framework is designed to steer systems toward sound judgment, human agency, and strict faithfulness to human intent. This update marks a significant step in defining operational and ethical standards for advanced AI models.
en.why_it_matters: Establishing clear specification frameworks helps bridge the gap between raw technological capability and responsible deployment. It provides stakeholders with insight into how companies plan to align sophisticated AI systems with human values.
en.extended_analysis:
As artificial intelligence systems grow increasingly capable and complex, the challenge of maintaining rigorous alignment and ethical guardrails becomes paramount. OpenAI's updated Model Spec addresses this by establishing five core values intended to direct model behavior toward sound judgment and respect for human agency.

Rather than focusing solely on raw benchmarks or performance metrics, this specification targets the qualitative aspects of AI decision-making. By emphasizing faithfulness to human intent, the framework attempts to mitigate risks related to unpredictable outputs and loss of human oversight.

Within the broader tech industry, the formalization of such specifications reflects a maturing approach to governance. Companies are increasingly pressed to articulate not just what their models can do, but the ethical and operational boundaries within which they operate.

Moving forward, analysts and developers will closely watch how these theoretical guidelines translate into practical model behavior, evaluating their effectiveness in real-world applications and deployment scenarios.
en.context: The introduction of updated model specifications occurs against a backdrop of intense global focus on AI safety, alignment, and governance standards. Developers are actively seeking frameworks to ensure advanced systems remain reliable and aligned with societal expectations.
key_takeaways: OpenAI introduced an updated Model Spec based on five core values.
The guidelines prioritize sound judgment, human agency, and intent faithfulness.
The initiative aims to guide the development of safer and more capable AI systems.
highlights: The Model Spec outlines five core values for AI guidance.
Published by OpenAI News in October 2026.

es.title: La nueva especificación de modelos de OpenAI para una IA beneficiosa
es.summary: OpenAI ha publicado una especificación de modelos actualizada que establece cinco valores fundamentales para guiar una inteligencia artificial más capaz. El documento busca orientar los sistemas hacia un juicio sólido, la agencia humana y la fidelidad a la intención del usuario. Esta iniciativa aporta directrices claras para el desarrollo responsable de la tecnología.
es.why_it_matters: Contar con especificaciones de modelos actualizadas es vital para alinear el progreso técnico con la seguridad y la ética. Ayuda a entender los mecanismos de control que las principales organizaciones implementan en sus sistemas avanzados.
es.extended_analysis:
A medida que la inteligencia artificial avanza hacia mayores niveles de capacidad, la necesidad de marcos normativos claros se vuelve imperativa. La actualización de la Model Spec de OpenAI introduce cinco valores clave concebidos para orientar el comportamiento de los modelos hacia un juicio sólido y el respeto por la agencia humana.

Este enfoque no solo aborda el rendimiento técnico, sino que prioriza la alineación cualitativa y la fidelidad a la intención humana. Al definir directrices precisas, se busca reducir los riesgos derivados de respuestas imprevistas o desalineadas con las expectativas de los usuarios.

En el contexto actual de la industria, la publicación de estas especificaciones refleja el esfuerzo continuo por formalizar estándares de gobernanza y seguridad. Los desarrolladores y reguladores examinan estos marcos para evaluar cómo se gestiona la complejidad de los modelos modernos.

En el futuro, será fundamental observar la aplicación práctica de estos valores en los sistemas desplegados y comprobar si logran traducirse en un comportamiento consistentemente seguro y beneficioso.
es.context: La publicación de especificaciones de modelos responde a la creciente presión regulatoria y social para garantizar que los sistemas de inteligencia artificial operen bajo estrictos estándares de seguridad y alineación ética.
key_takeaways: OpenAI actualiza su Model Spec en torno a cinco valores fundamentales.
Se prioriza la agencia humana, el juicio sólido y la fidelidad de intenciones.
El marco busca orientar el desarrollo de sistemas de IA más seguros y capaces.
highlights: La especificación define cinco valores esenciales para guiar la IA.
Información publicada por OpenAI News en octubre de 2026.

zh-CN.title: OpenAI发布更新版模型规范，推动更有能力且更有益的AI

该规范不仅关注基础的技术性能指标，更聚焦于模型决策的质量和对人类意图的忠实度。通过明确的导向，开发团队试图降低因模型行为偏离预期而带来的潜在风险，从而提升整体系统的可靠性。

未来，观察人士和技术人员将密切关注这些理论准则在真实场景中的执行效果，评估其是否能够有效引导AI系统朝着更加有益和安全的方向发展。

旨在为构建更安全、更具能力的人工智能系统提供指导。

Damit werden wesentliche Maßstäbe für die ethische und operative Ausrichtung fortschrittlicher Modelle gesetzt.

Angesichts der rasanten Entwicklung von Systemen der Künstlichen Intelligenz gewinnt die Frage der Ausrichtung und Governance zunehmend an Bedeutung. Die aktualisierte Modellspezifikation von OpenAI begegnet dieser Herausforderung mit fünf Kernwerten, die das Verhalten von Modellen gezielt steuern sollen.

Das Dokument konzentriert sich nicht nur auf technische Leistungskennzahlen, sondern adressiert qualitative Aspekte der Entscheidungsfindung. Durch die Betonung der Treue zur menschlichen Absicht und der Wahrung menschlicher Handlungsfähigkeit wird versucht, unvorhersehbare Risiken zu minimieren.

Im breiteren Branchenkontext spiegelt die Formalisierung solcher Leitlinien einen reiferen Umgang mit Sicherheitsfragen wider. Unternehmen müssen zunehmend demonstrieren, innerhalb welcher ethischen und operativen Grenzen ihre Technologien agieren.

Künftig wird es darauf ankommen zu beobachten, wie diese theoretischen Vorgaben in der Praxis implementiert werden und ob sie zu einer messbaren Verbesserung der Modellsicherheit und Zuverlässigkeit im Alltag führen.
de.context: Die Veröffentlichung aktualisierter Modellspezifikationen erfolgt vor dem Hintergrund globaler Bemühungen um mehr Sicherheit, Transparenz und ethische Standards bei der Entwicklung von generativen KI-Systemen.

en.title: How OpenAI detects frontier model misalignment

items.summary: In general, LLM performance is incredibly multidimensional. There's no guarantee of a fixed ordering where the model that is best at math is also the model that's best at jokes. Despite that complexity, much of the variation in performance is explained by just a single variable: model size. In general, models that are bigger will (a) be more performant / reliable, (b) cost more per token, and (c) have better recall of esoteric facts. As you note, our models are ordered: Luna < Terra < Sol < Astra [ ... ] These days, version number signifies a few things at once: the order of release, the relationship to other releases, and the magnitude of improvement. So something like 6.1 would indicate it was launched after 5.6, may share some similarities to other 6.1 models in terms of training data / personality (which is why it's not 5.7), and isn't a giant enough leap to merit the headlines and expectations that would come with a 7. — Ted Sanders , explaining OpenAI's model naming conventions Tags: generative-ai , gpt , openai , ai , llms , ted-sanders

GitHub Octoverse 2026
items.summary: GitHub Octoverse 2026 I'm at GitHub Universe today (GitHub gave me a free ticket through their "GitHub Stars" program). EVP Jay Parikh just announced this year's Octoverse report, and highlighted these numbers in particular: This is a pretty stark representation of the impact of agentic engineering on GitHub. In 2026, merged pull requests tripled in less than a year to 220 million per month. Commits more than tripled to 7.38 billion per month, with most of that increase in the second half of this year. New repository rate doubled this year, to 30.3 million per month. The report includes new numbers by industry, and breaks out numbers for repositories that involve "interoperability or reverse engineering". The methodology section includes notes about how they did this: Top countries by pushes to public repositories, adjusted by profile location . Pushes from each country were summed across the Octoverse year. To adjust for biases caused by VPN usage, LLM classification was used to extract the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code from the profiles of GitHub users who contributed pushes during this period [...] Industry . Public repositories created 2022 to 2026 were sorted into NAICS sectors by a fine-tuned multilingual embedding model using name, description, topics, and README, from random samples per year. [...] Interoperability . Counts public repositories created each year whose name, description, topics, or README mention interoperability or reverse engineering, or related terms, such as clean room implementation, drop-in replacement, or protocol re-implementation. Tags: github , ai , generative-ai , llms , coding-agents , disclosures , agentic-engineering

items.title: The October inflection point for vibe game development
items.summary: I've written before about how November 2025 was an inflection point for coding agents - the point where Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.1 crossed a tipping point that meant their respective coding agents became reliable daily drivers for software engineers. I think we've reached a new inflection point in October 2026, and this time it's for vibe coding computer games . Tree Appreciator Emberwick Battle Drones Pumpkin Farmer, aka Quarter Sun Cove Four times as insulting What happens if someone actually puts the work in? You should build a game! Claude Opus 5.5 in particular exhibits meaningful improvements in several areas needed to build a compelling game: 3D modeling Music generation (see Scrimshaw Jukebox ) Game design (!) That last one is particularly important. Models have been able to create something that looks like a game for quite a while now, as seen in my previous experiments . The challenge has been getting to a game that's actually fun to play . Game design is a deep subject area. I won't pretend to be well versed in it - I know enough to have respect for it as a craft. Creating a novel, compelling gameplay loop which challenges players at the right level and provides a satisfying learning curve is a fine art. I didn't think the models could do it. Then I tried telling Claude Opus 5.5 to "Make it a LOT more fun"... and it did . In the past few weeks I've vibe coded (in the classic sense of the term - no looking at the code at all) four games that I've genuinely enjoyed playing. I attended Foo Camp in Berkeley over the weekend and met several people who were having similar experiences. Building games that play well is shockingly easy now. items.title: Game Boy Color on My Conference Badge
items.summary: Game Boy Color on My Conference Badge I'm at GitHub Universe this week and, similar to last year , the conference badge is a full-blown color screen computer. I've been hacking around with it again, and then I ran into with Steve Francia... who worked with Gemini to get a full NES emulator working on it, and then went a step further and deployed an emulator for both the Game Boy and the Game Boy Color. Which means, if you can obtain the ROM, you can run The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening on your conference badge! A neat feature of the badge is that you can turn it upside down and then use game controller touch buttons that are built into the badge body. items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra
items.summary: GPT-6.1 Terra It's always interesting to note which aspects of a new model are emphasized in the release announcement. In the case of GPT-6.1 Terra, OpenAI went with visual reasoning and computer use: We’re introducing GPT-6.1 Terra , a fast, efficient model that combines detailed visual reasoning and precise computer use alongside clearer, more natural writing. A significant step up from GPT‑5.6 Terra, it excels at the communication and computer-based tasks that fill the workday, from drafting proposals and interpreting technical drawings to filling out forms and editing videos. Terra sits in the same position as Sonnet in the Anthropic model collection - not the cheapest or the most expensive, making it harder to decide when to use it. Computer use is a good example of a task that benefits from a less expensive model, since you might put it to work on automated, repetitive tasks. OpenAI's Ted Sanders provided some useful advice in a comment on Hacker News: In the case of GPT-6.1 Terra, I'd say Terra is probably better than Astra and Sol at technical communication, similar on vision and computer use (but much faster!), and a bit worse on most other things. For API developers, it's a nice midrange option if you want something cheaper than Sol but a lot smarter than Luna (especially for vision / computer use / communication). For subscribers, it's not a bombshell release - if you're hitting usage limits, maybe it helps you go a bit further, and if you want clearer communication or faster computer use, it can be a nice option to select. items.title: webframe: evaluated as a scraper and a sandbox
items.summary: Research: webframe: evaluated as a scraper and a sandbox webframe is a neat little project from Jeff Lindsay which lets you "run a web page like a program" - you point it at a URL or file and it executes it in a hidden headless web view and outputs console.log() to standard output and any exceptions to standard error. It's written in Go on top of the glaze library, which provides access to a system browser ("WKWebView on macOS, WebKitGTK on Linux, WebView2 on Windows") so it doesn't need to bundle its own browser engine. It reminds me of my own shot-scraper javascript tool, albeit in a much smaller package that doesn't depend on Playwright. I had Claude Opus 5.5 put it through its paces and prepare a research report for me. Here's the prompt I used: Explore https://github.com/tractordev/webframe try running it and put it though its paces, build a few exploratory prototypes, then evaluate it as a potential sandboxing tool and as a tool for scraping web pages using the same patterns encouraged by the "shot-scraper JavaScript" command (see simonw/shot-scraper on GitHub, docs directory) Tags: browsers , go , javascript , jeff-lindsay , shot-scraper

de.title: Ein Evaluierungssystem für KI-Wissenschaftler mit integriertem Lösungskey
de.summary: In dieser Episode des Podcasts Latent Space spricht Ian Quigley von Leash Bio über ein neuartiges Evaluierungssystem für KI-Wissenschaftler, das mit einem festen Lösungskey ausgestattet ist. Da die verfügbare Beschreibung äußerst knapp gehalten ist, werden Hörer auf die vollständige Show auf YouTube verwiesen. Das Gespräch bietet einen vorsichtigen Einblick in die Methoden zur Leistungs- und Genauigkeitsmessung von KI in der Forschung.
de.why_it_matters: Die Entwicklung verlässlicher Evaluierungsmethoden für KI-gestützte wissenschaftliche Werkzeuge ist entscheidend, um deren tatsächliche Leistungsfähigkeit zu überprüfen. Diese Episode beleuchtet die laufenden Bemühungen, strukturierte Benchmarks mit klaren Validierungsschlüsseln in komplexen Forschungsbereichen zu etablieren.
de.extended_analysis:
Die von Latent Space präsentierte Konversation mit Ian Quigley von Leash Bio widmet sich der zentralen Herausforderung, künstliche Intelligenz in wissenschaftlichen Arbeitsabläufen zu bewerten. Da automatisierte Systeme zunehmend in Disziplinen wie die Wirkstoffforschung und Biologie vordringen, bleibt die Etablierung verlässlicher Bewertungsstandards eine wichtige Hürde für Entwickler.

Die vorliegenden Metadaten dieser Episode sind sehr kurz gefasst und enthalten lediglich einen Verweis auf das vollständige Video bei YouTube, ohne technische Details zur Implementierung oder Benchmark-Architektur zu nennen. Aussagen über die Leistungsfähigkeit müssen daher im Rahmen der vom Gast vorgestellten Themen betrachtet werden.

Da das Fachgebiet die automatisierte wissenschaftliche Entdeckung weiter vorantreibt, bleibt die Beobachtung solcher Evaluierungsansätze von großer Bedeutung. Interessierte sollten zukünftige Veröffentlichungen und Diskussionen verfolgen, um die praktischen Auswirkungen dieser Bewertungsmodelle besser einzuordnen.
de.context: Der Podcast Latent Space widmet sich regelmäßig technischen Fortschritten in der KI-Entwicklung und angewandten Forschung. Die Episode reiht sich in den technischen Diskurs über wissenschaftliche Benchmarks und Modellevaluierung ein.
key_takeaways: Ian Quigley von Leash Bio ist zu Gast in der Episode.
Im Mittelpunkt steht ein Evaluierungsansatz für KI-Wissenschaftler mit Lösungskey.
Die offizielle Beschreibung verweist auf die vollständige Videoaufzeichnung auf YouTube.

items.sourceEvidence: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro, our most capable 3T-class open-weight model with 1M-token context and major advances in coding, 3D modeling, and financial research. it.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro punta su contesto lungo e pesi aperti
it.summary: Moonshot presenta Kimi K3.1 Pro, un modello open-weight da 3 trilioni di parametri con una finestra di contesto da un milione di token. La variante Highspeed promette una velocità 2–3 volte maggiore; l’azienda annuncia il rilascio dei pesi completi entro il 4 novembre. I benchmark pubblicati sono risultati dichiarati da Moonshot, da confrontare con test indipendenti.
it.why_it_matters: Un modello di queste dimensioni, con pesi destinati alla pubblicazione, può ampliare la sperimentazione su coding e agenti. Il valore pratico dipenderà però da licenza, requisiti hardware e verifiche indipendenti, non solo dai benchmark del produttore.
it.extended_analysis:
Kimi K3.1 Pro è il nuovo modello di punta annunciato da Moonshot AI. La società lo descrive come un sistema open-weight da 3T di parametri, capace di gestire fino a un milione di token di contesto. Accanto alla versione standard arriva K3.1 Pro Highspeed, presentata come 2–3 volte più veloce.

La pagina ufficiale riporta risultati su coding, ricerca finanziaria e attività agentiche, tra cui 65,7% su Terminal-Bench 4.0. Sono valutazioni comunicate dal produttore: per capire quanto siano riproducibili servono pesi, metodologia completa e confronti indipendenti. Moonshot indica il 4 novembre per la pubblicazione dei pesi completi; sarà quello il passaggio decisivo per valutare accessibilità, costi di esecuzione e possibilità di adattamento.
it.context: I modelli open-weight permettono a sviluppatori e organizzazioni di esaminare e distribuire i pesi, entro i termini della licenza. Una finestra di contesto molto ampia è utile per documenti e flussi di lavoro lunghi, ma aumenta anche i requisiti di memoria e calcolo.
key_takeaways: Contesto dichiarato: fino a 1 milione di token.
La variante Highspeed promette 2–3× la velocità.
Pesi completi annunciati entro il 4 novembre; benchmark da verificare indipendentemente.
highlights: Modello open-weight da 3T di parametri, secondo Moonshot.
Disponibile anche una variante Highspeed.
I risultati citati provengono dalla valutazione pubblicata dall’azienda.

en.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro pushes long context and open weights
en.summary: Moonshot introduces Kimi K3.1 Pro, a 3-trillion-parameter open-weight model with a one-million-token context window. Its Highspeed variant is claimed to run 2–3 times faster, while full weights are scheduled for release by November 4. The published benchmark figures are company-reported results and still need independent scrutiny.
en.why_it_matters: A model of this scale, with weights intended for release, could broaden experimentation in coding and agent workflows. Its practical value will depend on licensing, hardware requirements and independent evaluation—not just the vendor’s benchmarks.
en.extended_analysis:
Kimi K3.1 Pro is the new flagship model announced by Moonshot AI. The company describes it as a 3T-parameter open-weight system with a context window of up to one million tokens. A Highspeed variant is also offered, with a claimed 2–3× speed improvement.

The official post reports results across coding, financial research and agentic tasks, including 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0. These are figures published by the vendor; reproducibility will depend on the released weights, full methodology and independent comparisons. Moonshot says the complete weights are due by November 4. That release will be the real test of accessibility, serving costs and how easily developers can adapt the model.
en.context: Open-weight models let developers and organisations inspect and run model weights, subject to the licence. Very long context can help with large documents and multi-step workflows, but it also raises memory and compute demands.
key_takeaways: Advertised context window: up to one million tokens.
Highspeed is claimed to be 2–3× faster.
Full weights are expected by November 4; benchmarks remain vendor-reported.
highlights: A 3T-parameter open-weight model, according to Moonshot.
A faster Highspeed variant is also announced.
Published performance figures have not been independently validated here.

La variante Highspeed promete ser entre 2 y 3 veces más rápida; la empresa prevé publicar los pesos completos antes del 4 de noviembre. es.why_it_matters: Un modelo de esta escala, con pesos destinados a publicarse, puede ampliar la experimentación en programación y agentes. Su utilidad real dependerá de la licencia, el hardware necesario y las evaluaciones independientes, no solo de los benchmarks de la empresa.
es.extended_analysis:
Kimi K3.1 Pro es el nuevo modelo insignia anunciado por Moonshot AI. La compañía lo describe como un sistema de pesos abiertos de 3T de parámetros, con una ventana de contexto de hasta un millón de tokens. También presenta una variante Highspeed, a la que atribuye una velocidad entre dos y tres veces superior.

La publicación oficial recoge resultados en programación, investigación financiera y tareas con agentes, incluido un 65,7 % en Terminal-Bench 4.0. Son cifras comunicadas por el fabricante: su reproducibilidad dependerá de los pesos publicados, de la metodología completa y de comparaciones independientes. es.context: Los modelos de pesos abiertos permiten examinar y ejecutar los pesos, siempre dentro de las condiciones de su licencia. Un contexto muy amplio puede ayudar con documentos extensos y procesos de varios pasos, pero también exige más memoria y capacidad de cálculo.

Highspeed promete entre 2 y 3 veces más velocidad.
Los pesos completos se esperan para el 4 de noviembre; los benchmarks son del fabricante.

de.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro setzt auf langen Kontext und offene Gewichte
de.summary: Moonshot stellt Kimi K3.1 Pro vor: ein Open-Weight-Modell mit 3 Billionen Parametern und einem Kontextfenster von einer Million Tokens. Die Highspeed-Variante soll zwei- bis dreimal schneller sein; die vollständigen Gewichte sollen bis zum 4. November folgen. Die veröffentlichten Benchmarkwerte stammen vom Anbieter und müssen unabhängig überprüft werden.
de.why_it_matters: Ein Modell dieser Größe mit frei verfügbaren Gewichten könnte Experimente mit Coding und Agenten-Workflows erleichtern. Der praktische Nutzen hängt jedoch von Lizenz, Hardwarebedarf und unabhängigen Tests ab – nicht allein von den Benchmarks des Herstellers.
de.extended_analysis:
Kimi K3.1 Pro ist das neue Spitzenmodell, das Moonshot AI angekündigt hat. Das Unternehmen beschreibt es als Open-Weight-System mit 3 Billionen Parametern und einem Kontextfenster von bis zu einer Million Tokens. Zusätzlich gibt es eine Highspeed-Version, die laut Anbieter zwei- bis dreimal schneller arbeitet.

Der offizielle Beitrag nennt Ergebnisse für Coding, Finanzrecherche und agentische Aufgaben, darunter 65,7 Prozent auf Terminal-Bench 4.0. Diese Zahlen wurden vom Hersteller veröffentlicht; ihre Reproduzierbarkeit hängt von den verfügbaren Gewichten, der vollständigen Methodik und unabhängigen Vergleichen ab. Moonshot stellt die vollständigen Gewichte bis zum 4. November in Aussicht. Erst dann lassen sich Zugänglichkeit, Betriebskosten und Anpassungsmöglichkeiten besser beurteilen.
de.context: Open-Weight-Modelle erlauben Entwicklern und Organisationen, Gewichte im Rahmen der Lizenz zu prüfen und auszuführen. Ein sehr langes Kontextfenster hilft bei großen Dokumenten und mehrstufigen Aufgaben, erhöht aber auch den Speicher- und Rechenbedarf.
key_takeaways: Angegebenes Kontextfenster: bis zu einer Million Tokens.
Highspeed soll zwei- bis dreimal schneller sein.
Vollständige Gewichte bis 4. November angekündigt; Benchmarks sind Anbieterangaben.

items.summary: State-of-the-art probabilistic forecasting in four sizes (5M–209M params), CPU-efficient, zero-shot ready.
items.sourceEvidence: State-of-the-art probabilistic forecasting in four sizes (5M–209M params), CPU-efficient, zero-shot ready. Timestral: Mistral's time-series foundation models | Mistral Get in touch Menu Research Sovereign AI Cloud Customers Company Get in touch Start building Why Sovereign AI Products Method Sovereign AI in practice Inference Compute Energy & utilities Manufacturing Financial services Public sector Cybersecurity All customers Blog Docs About us Careers Research Sovereign AI Cloud Customers Company Why Sovereign AI Products Method Sovereign AI in practice Inference Compute Energy & utilities Manufacturing Financial services Public sector Cybersecurity All customers Blog Docs About us Careers Get in touch --> Start building Studio Vibe Pricing Research Introducing Timestral October 15, 2026 By Mistral Back to Blog 7 min read Share this post Copy url to clipboard Copied Thinking Summary Timestral, Mistral’s first family of time-series foundation models, delivers state-of-the-art probabilistic, multivariate forecasts with just 209M parameters, outperforming larger models on key benchmarks while supporting past and future covariates. Available in four sizes (5M to 209M parameters), it balances accuracy and efficiency, running efficiently on CPUs and excelling in zero-shot forecasting for diverse domains. The model combines synthetic pre-training, covariate-aware attention, and long-context learning, with fine-tuning options for domain adaptation via Mistral Forge. Today, we’re releasing Timestral, our first family of time-series foundation models. Our largest model, at just 209M parameters, ranks first on all three of the field's main public benchmarks, GIFT-Eval, TIME, and fev-bench, outperforming the previous state of the art with only two-thirds of the model parameters. Timestral delivers probabilistic, multivariate forecasts and supports past-only and known-future covariates. Our family of models sits on the Pareto front of forecasting accuracy versus model size, delivering leading performance at each size. Results have been submitted to the GIFT-Eval and TIME leaderboards. Time Series Foundation Models (TSFM) Time series is one of the most common data types in enterprise, from sensor telemetry to observability metrics. Forecasts built on it drive decisions in capacity planning, energy, supply chains, risk and maintenance. Industrial plants forecast process sensors against the production schedule, catch equipment drift before it fails, and plan capacity and spare parts across thousands of assets. Finance teams forecast flows, volumes, and volatility to inform positions, hedging, and treasury across thousands of accounts. Classical models such as ARIMA and linear regression remain well-established tools for forecasting time series. These models are usually fitted to a single series and learn only from that series' history. Deep learning models such as PatchTST add the capacity to learn nonlinear patterns across many related series, but they are still typically trained from scratch on each dataset, so what they learn doesn't carry over to new domains. Time series foundation models bring the pre-training approach to time series. Trained on a large and diverse corpus, our model learns patterns that transfer across series, forecasting zero-shot on data it has never seen, even in domains where data is scarce. Benchmark Results We evaluated Timestral on the three main public forecasting benchmarks: GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench. Among pre-trained, zero-shot models, it ranks first across all five metrics. These results come from a single checkpoint, without ensembling. it.title: Timestral: modelli compatti per prevedere dati che cambiano nel tempo
it.summary: Mistral presenta Timestral, una famiglia di modelli per previsioni su serie temporali in quattro dimensioni, da 5 a 209 milioni di parametri. L’azienda dichiara risultati ai vertici di benchmark pubblici e inferenza su CPU: l’obiettivo è rendere più accessibili previsioni probabilistiche e multivariate in ambiti come manutenzione, energia e finanza.
it.why_it_matters: Molte decisioni operative dipendono da dati che evolvono nel tempo. Modelli relativamente piccoli, capaci di stimare più variabili e l’incertezza delle previsioni, potrebbero rendere queste tecniche più praticabili anche fuori dai grandi cluster GPU.
it.extended_analysis:
Timestral è la prima famiglia di foundation model di Mistral dedicata alle serie temporali. La gamma comprende quattro taglie, da 5 a 209 milioni di parametri, e punta su previsioni probabilistiche e multivariate: non un solo valore futuro, ma una distribuzione di scenari e relazioni tra più segnali.

Mistral dichiara il primo posto su GIFT-Eval, TIME e fev-bench per i modelli pre-addestrati valutati in modalità zero-shot. L’azienda indica inoltre tempi di inferenza su CPU standard e l’uso di variabili note in anticipo, come calendari o programmi di produzione. Sono risultati e misure pubblicati dal produttore: per valutarne l’utilità concreta serviranno test sui dati e sui vincoli dei singoli settori.
it.context: Le serie temporali descrivono fenomeni misurati nel tempo: consumi, sensori industriali, domanda, prezzi e metriche operative. Un foundation model pre-addestrato cerca di trasferire schemi appresi da molti dataset a nuove serie, riducendo la necessità di addestrare da zero ogni singolo modello.
key_takeaways: Quattro versioni: 5M, 28M, 123M e 209M parametri.
Previsioni multivariate e probabilistiche, con variabili passate e future note.
Mistral dichiara inferenza su CPU e risultati di benchmark da verificare sui casi d’uso reali.
highlights: Prima famiglia di modelli Timestral di Mistral.
Progettata per forecasting zero-shot su serie nuove.
Il produttore pubblica benchmark e tempi CPU.

en.title: Timestral brings compact foundation models to time-series forecasting
en.summary: Mistral introduces Timestral, a family of time-series forecasting models in four sizes, from 5M to 209M parameters. The company reports leading results on public benchmarks and CPU inference, aiming to make probabilistic, multivariate forecasts more practical for areas such as maintenance, energy and finance.
en.why_it_matters: Operational decisions often depend on signals that change over time. Relatively small models that estimate multiple variables and forecast uncertainty could make advanced forecasting more accessible beyond GPU-heavy infrastructure.
en.extended_analysis:
Timestral is Mistral’s first family of foundation models designed for time series. It comes in four sizes, from 5M to 209M parameters, and focuses on probabilistic, multivariate forecasts: rather than outputting a single future value, it can estimate a range of outcomes and relationships among signals.

Mistral says the models lead GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench among pretrained models evaluated in zero-shot settings. The company also reports CPU inference times and support for known-future inputs such as calendars and production schedules. These are vendor-published claims and measurements; their practical value will need to be tested against the data, latency and reliability requirements of each domain.
en.context: Time series describe measurements over time, including energy use, industrial sensors, demand, prices and operational metrics. A pretrained foundation model aims to transfer patterns learned from many datasets to new series, reducing the need to train a separate model from scratch for every use case.
key_takeaways: Four sizes: 5M, 28M, 123M and 209M parameters.
Probabilistic, multivariate forecasts with past and known-future covariates.
Mistral reports CPU inference and benchmark results that still need real-world validation.
highlights: Mistral’s first Timestral time-series model family.
Designed for zero-shot forecasting on unseen series.
The vendor publishes benchmark results and CPU timings.

es.title: Timestral lleva modelos compactos a la predicción de series temporales
es.summary: Mistral presenta Timestral, una familia de modelos para predecir series temporales en cuatro tamaños, de 5 a 209 millones de parámetros. La empresa afirma lograr resultados destacados en benchmarks públicos y ejecutar inferencias en CPU, con el objetivo de facilitar previsiones probabilísticas y multivariantes en mantenimiento, energía y finanzas.
es.why_it_matters: Muchas decisiones operativas dependen de señales que cambian con el tiempo. Modelos relativamente pequeños capaces de estimar varias variables y la incertidumbre podrían acercar estas técnicas a organizaciones sin grandes infraestructuras GPU.
es.extended_analysis:
Timestral es la primera familia de modelos fundacionales de Mistral dedicada a las series temporales. Incluye cuatro tamaños, de 5 a 209 millones de parámetros, y se centra en previsiones probabilísticas y multivariantes: no ofrece solo un valor futuro, sino un conjunto de escenarios y relaciones entre señales.

Mistral afirma liderar GIFT-Eval, TIME y fev-bench entre los modelos preentrenados evaluados en modo zero-shot. La compañía también publica tiempos de inferencia en CPU y soporte para variables futuras conocidas, como calendarios y planes de producción. Son resultados y mediciones comunicados por el fabricante; su utilidad deberá comprobarse con los datos, la latencia y los requisitos de fiabilidad de cada sector.
es.context: Las series temporales representan mediciones a lo largo del tiempo: consumo energético, sensores industriales, demanda, precios y métricas operativas. Un modelo fundacional preentrenado intenta transferir patrones aprendidos de muchos conjuntos de datos a nuevas series y reducir la necesidad de entrenar un modelo desde cero para cada caso.
key_takeaways: Cuatro tamaños: 5M, 28M, 123M y 209M parámetros.
Predicciones probabilísticas y multivariantes con variables pasadas y futuras conocidas.
Mistral publica resultados de benchmarks y tiempos en CPU que deben validarse en casos reales.
highlights: Primera familia Timestral de Mistral para series temporales.
Diseñada para predicción zero-shot en series nuevas.
El fabricante publica benchmarks y tiempos de CPU.

zh-CN.title: Timestral：让轻量模型也能进行时间序列预测
zh-CN.summary: Mistral 推出 Timestral 时间序列模型家族，提供 5M 至 209M 参数的四种规格。公司称其在公开基准测试中表现领先，并可在 CPU 上运行，目标是让维护、能源和金融等领域更容易使用概率式、多变量预测。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 许多运营决策都依赖随时间变化的数据。能够同时预测多个变量并表达不确定性的轻量模型，有望降低高级预测技术对大型 GPU 基础设施的依赖。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
Timestral 是 Mistral 首个专为时间序列设计的基础模型家族，共有四种规格，参数量从 5M 到 209M。它强调概率式、多变量预测：模型不只给出一个未来数值，还尝试描述可能结果的范围以及不同信号之间的关系。

Mistral 表示，在预训练模型的 zero-shot 评测中，Timestral 在 GIFT-Eval、TIME 和 fev-bench 上取得领先成绩。公司还公布了 CPU 推理速度，并支持日历、生产计划等已知未来变量。这些属于厂商发布的结果和测量，实际效果仍需结合各行业的数据、延迟和可靠性要求进行验证。
zh-CN.context: 时间序列是按时间连续记录的数据，例如能源消耗、工业传感器、需求、价格和运营指标。预训练基础模型希望把从大量数据集中学到的规律迁移到新的序列，减少每个场景都从头训练模型的需求。
key_takeaways: 提供 5M、28M、123M 和 209M 四种规格。
支持概率式、多变量预测及已知未来协变量。
CPU 运行和基准成绩来自厂商公布，仍需真实场景检验。
highlights: Mistral 首个时间序列 Timestral 模型家族。
面向未见过的数据进行 zero-shot 预测。
官方公布了基准成绩和 CPU 推理时间。

de.title: Timestral bringt kompakte Foundation-Modelle in die Zeitreihenprognose
de.summary: Mistral stellt Timestral vor, eine Familie von Zeitreihenmodellen in vier Größen von 5 bis 209 Millionen Parametern. Das Unternehmen meldet Spitzenwerte auf öffentlichen Benchmarks und Inferenz auf CPUs. Damit sollen probabilistische Prognosen über mehrere Variablen etwa in Wartung, Energie und Finanzwesen leichter nutzbar werden.
de.why_it_matters: Viele operative Entscheidungen hängen von Signalen ab, die sich laufend verändern. Relativ kleine Modelle, die mehrere Variablen und die Unsicherheit einer Prognose erfassen, könnten fortgeschrittene Vorhersagen auch ohne große GPU-Infrastruktur praktikabler machen.
de.extended_analysis:
Timestral ist Mistrals erste Foundation-Model-Familie für Zeitreihen. Sie umfasst vier Größen von 5 bis 209 Millionen Parametern und zielt auf probabilistische Prognosen über mehrere Variablen. Statt nur einen zukünftigen Wert auszugeben, soll das Modell mögliche Szenarien und Beziehungen zwischen Signalen abbilden.

Mistral zufolge liegt Timestral bei GIFT-Eval, TIME und fev-bench unter den vortrainierten Zero-Shot-Modellen vorn. Das Unternehmen veröffentlicht außerdem CPU-Laufzeiten und Unterstützung für bekannte zukünftige Eingaben wie Kalender oder Produktionspläne. Diese Ergebnisse und Messwerte stammen vom Anbieter; ihr praktischer Nutzen muss mit den Daten, Latenz- und Zuverlässigkeitsanforderungen der jeweiligen Branche geprüft werden.
de.context: Zeitreihen beschreiben Messwerte im Verlauf der Zeit, etwa Energieverbrauch, Industriesensoren, Nachfrage, Preise und Betriebskennzahlen. Ein vortrainiertes Foundation-Modell soll Muster aus vielen Datensätzen auf neue Reihen übertragen und damit das Training eines separaten Modells für jeden Anwendungsfall verringern.
key_takeaways: Vier Größen: 5M, 28M, 123M und 209M Parameter.
Probabilistische Prognosen über mehrere Variablen mit vergangenen und bekannten zukünftigen Einflussgrößen.
CPU-Laufzeiten und Benchmarkwerte sind Herstellerangaben und müssen im Einsatz geprüft werden.
highlights: Mistrals erste Timestral-Modellfamilie für Zeitreihen.
Für Zero-Shot-Prognosen auf unbekannten Daten ausgelegt.
Der Hersteller veröffentlicht Benchmarks und CPU-Zeiten.

items.title: Airbnb Is Building a ‘Company Brain’ for AI Agents with Ahmad Al-Dahle - #781
items.summary: AI agents need the institutional knowledge experienced employees rely on: why a system works a certain way, which policies apply, and what never made it into the documentation. Capturing that knowledge is hard. Keeping it useful as people and agents add more may be harder. In this episode, Ahmad Al-Dahle, CTO of Airbnb, shares how his team is building Project Everest, a “company brain” that captures knowledge from employees’ workflows for AI agents. We explore stale information and context poisoning, why too much context can backfire, and how the team evaluates whether shared knowledge improves engineering work. We also discuss measuring AI productivity beyond token usage and PR counts, the limits of chat-based interfaces, and deploying support agents in a marketplace where resolving disputes means mediating between conflicting interests. 🗒️ Full show notes: https://twimlai.com/go/781.
